scope.explanation: Use evidence to choose parameter, causal-feature, permitted device-weight, or composite controls. Labels, sampling, feature_set, schedule and scorer remain fixed.

feature_api.input: One device, chronological numeric rows. No labels, device IDs or future rows. Select literal column names from profile.feature_names.
feature_api.output: pd.DataFrame of declared unique fe_ columns; preserve rows and index. Original columns are retained automatically.

past_helpers.past.gap_seconds(frame): Series: current minus previous observation time in seconds; first value NaN.
past_helpers.past.observation_count(frame): Series: causal count 1,2,...,n; no measured-value missingness dependence.

rules: Only assignments to new local names and a final return. No loops, comprehensions, imports or arbitrary functions.
frame.index is permitted ONLY as index=frame.index in pd.DataFrame. For time gaps use past.gap_seconds(frame).
No frame.columns, to_series, dt, iloc, loc, values, pd.Series, pd.to_numeric or apply. Inputs are already numeric.
Use arithmetic operators / + - * instead of .div/.add/.sub/.mul. Use literal column names; never discover columns dynamically.
Reductions must directly follow rolling/expanding/ewm. Use trailing real-time rolling windows; center=True and negative shifts are forbidden.
Missing measurements stay unknown unless the hypothesis explicitly justifies a constant or forward fill. No infinities.
Zero finite values in a bounded sample is a coverage limitation, not evidence that the entire dataset is empty.

hypotheses.mechanism: Accumulating correctable errors across all sources reflect progressive cell or row wear and increase pre-fault risk.
hypotheses.basis: DRAM cell wear-out and variable retention time often appear first as rising correctable error counts before uncorrectable faults.
hypotheses.falsified_if: Failing devices do not show elevated aggregate CE counts or log counts relative to healthy devices in the same pre-fault windows.

hypotheses.mechanism: Burst errors, where multiple errors occur close together in time or space, indicate clustered defect activation and higher failure probability.
hypotheses.basis: Clustered correctable errors are a known sign of localized damage such as weak rows, partial wordline failure, or degraded sense amplifiers.
hypotheses.falsified_if: Failing devices have similar or lower burst counts than healthy devices.

hypotheses.mechanism: CE storm events represent sudden high-rate error bursts and are precursors of uncorrectable faults.
hypotheses.basis: Operational experience shows that CE storms often precede DRAM failures, especially when combined with row or bank faults.
hypotheses.falsified_if: CE storm frequency is not higher in failing devices before the fault window.

hypotheses.mechanism: DQ-related error counts reflect degraded data integrity or I/O margin and predict failure.
hypotheses.basis: Data quality or data path errors often accompany cell and sense amplifier degradation in failing DRAM devices.
hypotheses.falsified_if: DQ-related error counts are not elevated among failing devices relative to healthy devices.

hypotheses.mechanism: Scrub-detected errors reveal background latent defects; higher scrub CE counts or log counts indicate a larger hidden error population.
hypotheses.basis: Patrol scrub surfaces retention and variable retention time errors that are not triggered by normal reads and are associated with cell wear.
hypotheses.falsified_if: Failing devices do not show higher scrub-detected CE counts or log counts than healthy devices.

hypotheses.mechanism: Read-path correctable errors indicate read-disturb or weak-cell failures and are elevated before DRAM faults.
hypotheses.basis: Read operations can disturb weak cells; higher read CE counts suggest marginal cells that may fail under continued use.
hypotheses.falsified_if: Read CE counts or log counts do not differ between failing and healthy devices.

hypotheses.mechanism: Shorter maximum intervals between bursts or DQ events reflect persistent instability and higher failure risk.
hypotheses.basis: A narrow maximum interval indicates recurring error activity rather than isolated transient events, which is more consistent with progressive defect growth.
hypotheses.falsified_if: Maximum intervals are not shorter in failing devices than in healthy devices.

hypotheses.mechanism: Higher logged error event frequency is associated with imminent failure.
hypotheses.basis: More frequent CE or error log events indicate an active, worsening defect population rather than stable background errors.
hypotheses.falsified_if: Failing devices have similar or lower logged error frequency than healthy devices.

hypotheses.mechanism: Spatial fault mode distribution differentiates failing devices: row and column modes suggest wordline/bitline defects, while bank- or device-wide modes indicate more systemic failure.
hypotheses.basis: DRAM failure modes have distinct physical signatures; localized row/column faults often precede peripheral or systemic failures.
hypotheses.falsified_if: Failing devices do not show a distinct fault mode distribution from healthy devices; row/column modes are not more prevalent among failing devices.

hypotheses.mechanism: The number of distinct faulty rows, columns, or error bits increases as failure progresses.
hypotheses.basis: Growing unique fault locations indicate expanding defect scope and higher probability of uncorrectable failure.
hypotheses.falsified_if: Failing devices do not show more unique faulty rows, columns, or error bits than healthy devices.

hypotheses.mechanism: Error burst and error DQ counts represent uncorrectable or multi-bit integrity failures and are elevated before device failure.
hypotheses.basis: Multi-bit and DQ-path errors are more severe than isolated correctable errors and can indicate imminent uncorrectable faults.
hypotheses.falsified_if: Error burst or error DQ counts are not elevated in failing devices before the fault window.

acceptance_rule.explanation: best changes only when paired CV bootstrap P(better) >= 0.9 and CV F1 gain > lower_bound

task_context.instructions: Domain-adapted evidence loop: separate false alarms, missed faults and coverage; allow bounded interaction/recall feature exploration, single-factor device weights and optional independent parallel branch. Reuse the source sampling policy and fixed evaluation. New source/representation requires a new cache/session. TEST stays outside search. TypeB only. Use supplied baseline features; do not infer healthy labels beyond May 2024.
